questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant deployment patterns, including per-tenant isolation, feature flag management, and automated quality gates in enterprise environments.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- AKS with per-tenant namespaces
- App Configuration for feature flags
- k6 synthetic testing
- Azure Monitor logging
- Per-tenant promotion gates with automated rollback

## Code Example

```yaml
name: MultiTenantCanary
trigger: none
stages:
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployTenant
    strategy:
      matrix:
        tenantA: { tenant: 'tenant-a' }
        tenantB: { tenant: 'tenant-b' }
    environment: 'aks-${tenant}'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Deploy to AKS namespace'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --resource-group $(rgName) --name $(aksCluster)
                kubectl set image deployment/api api=$(containerImage) --namespace=$(tenant)
          - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
            displayName: 'Fetch feature flags'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              appConfigurationResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              appConfigurationName: '$(appConfigName)'
              label: '$(tenant)'
          - task: Bash@3
            displayName: 'Run k6 synthetic tests'
            env:
              TENANT_URL: 'https://$(tenant).api.example.com'
            inputs:
              filePath: 'tests/k6-synthetic.sh'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Check health and gate promotion'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s https://$(tenant).api.example.com/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed for $(tenant)"
                  exit 1
                fi
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Rollback on failure'
            condition: failed()
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                kubectl rollout undo deployment/api --namespace=$(tenant)
                echo "Rolled back $(tenant) to previous revision"
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
            inputs:
              azureResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              resourceType: 'Container Insights'
```

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical Azure DevOps skills, blue/green deployment, per-environment secrets/flags, and safe rollback in a beginner-friendly scenario.

## Key Concepts

- YAML multi-stage pipelines
- Helm deployments in AKS with namespace isolation
- Azure App Configuration feature flags per environment
- Azure Key Vault secrets integration
- Traffic-switching and rollback safety
- Monitoring/logging with Azure Monitor

## Code Example

```yaml
# skeleton
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
    - main

stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '18.x'
    - script: npm install
    - script: npm test
- stage: Publish
  jobs:
  - job: BuildAndPush
    steps:
    - script: docker build -t <acr>/api:$(Build.BuildId) .
    - script: docker push <acr>/api:$(Build.BuildId)
- stage: DeployBlue
  jobs:
  - job: DeployBlue
    steps:
    - script: helm upgrade --install api-blue charts/api --namespace blue --set image.tag=$(Build.BuildId)
- stage: SmokeTest
  jobs:
  - job: Smoke
    steps:
    - script: ./scripts/smoke-test.sh
- stage: Promote
  dependsOn: SmokeTest
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
  - job: Promote
    steps:
    - task: ManualValidation@0
      inputs:
        instructions: 'Approve prod swap if blue is healthy'
- stage: Rollback
  dependsOn: Promote
  condition: failed()
  jobs:
  - job: Rollback
    steps:
    - script: helm upgrade --install api-green charts/api --namespace green --set image.tag=$(Build.BuildId)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle secret rotation in this setup?
- How would you test the blue/green rollback in a CI environment?

## Code Example
```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml - PR-driven ephemeral deployment pipeline
trigger:
  none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - main

variables:
  - group: azure-infrastructure
  - name: prNumber
    value: $(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
  - name: prTag
    value: 'pr-$(prNumber)'

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  displayName: 'Detect Changed Services'
  jobs:
  - job: detect
    steps:
    - bash: |
        git diff origin/main --name-only > changed_files.txt
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedServices;isOutput=true]$(python detect-services.py changed_files.txt)"
      name: detect

- stage: BuildAndPush
  displayName: 'Build and Push Services'
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
  - job: build
    strategy:
      matrix: $[ stageDependencies.DetectChanges.detect.outputs['detect.changedServices'] ]
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        containerRegistry: $(acrServiceConnection)
        repository: $(service.name)
        tags: |
          $(prTag)
          $(Build.BuildNumber)
        command: buildAndPush
        Dockerfile: $(service.path)/Dockerfile
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- Azure App Service deployment slots (staging/production) and slot swap
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment flags
- Health checks and rollback strategies
- Logging/auditing to Azure Monitor / Log Analytics
- Service connections and least-privilege access

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest
variables:
  imageName: myapi
  registry: <ACR_NAME>.azurecr.io
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs: {version: '18.x'}
    - script: npm install
    - script: npm test
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: Deploy
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerRegistry: '<registry-service-connection>'
        repository: '$(registry)/$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: |
          $(Build.BuildId)
    - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        appName: '<app-service-name>'
        imageName: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
        resourceGroup: '<rg>'
        slotName: 'staging'
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        script: |
          HEALTH_URL=https://<app-service-name>-staging.azurewebsites.net/health
          if curl -sSf $HEALTH_URL | grep -q 'ok'; then
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot staging --target-slot production
          else
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot production --target-slot staging
            exit 1
          fi
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates knowledge of ephemeral PR environments, Azure DevOps pipelines, and Infrastructure as Code orchestration patterns.

## Key Concepts
- PR-triggered pipeline automation
- Azure Container Instances for temporary environments
- Azure Key Vault and App Configuration integration
- Health monitoring and drift detection
- Cost-conscious cleanup strategies and centralized logging

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example skeleton (illustrates core structure)
trigger:
  none
pr:
  autoCancel: true
jobs:
- job: PRPreview
  displayName: 'PR Preview Environment'
  pool:
    vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
  steps:
  - task: AzureCLI@2
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: '<service-connection>'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        # Provision ACI with unique name
        az container create \
          --name api-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber) \
          --resource-group <resource-group> \
          --image <acr-repo>/api:pr-$(Build.BuildId)
```
